chunks: 3. Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakklin (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Ali ibn Ibrahim said: Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd narrated from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Abd Allah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
He said: I asked him about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'The nature of Allah which He created people upon.' What is that nature?
He said: It is Islam. Allah created them upon it when He took their covenant regarding Divine Unity, saying: 'Am I not your Lord?' And in it are the believer and the disbeliever.

key_terms.فِطْرَة: Natural disposition or innate nature created by God

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Fitrah in Shia theology according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq identifies 'fitrah' as Islam, specifically the innate recognition of Tawhid, linking it to the primordial covenant (Mithaq) where all souls acknowledged God as Lord. This interpretation emphasizes that belief is not merely acquired but rooted in an inherent, universal disposition established at creation, distinguishing the state of the believer and disbeliever based on their adherence to this innate truth.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 3. Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (RA) said: `Ali ibn Ibrahim said: Muhammad ibn `Isa ibn `Ubayd said, on the authority of Yunus ibn `Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of `Abd Allah ibn Sinan
that I asked Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) “What is the nature referred to in the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: “The nature made by Allah is which He has made men.”

He responded, It is Islam. Allah placed this nature in them when He created them and made a covenant with them regarding Divine Unity. Thus, He asked: Am I not your Lord? The covenant encompassed all those who believe and all those who disbelieve.
